name: Real Estate & Construction
eyebrow: Automation for developers, brokers, commercial landlords, co-working and contractors
headline: Fewer cold leads. Fewer surprises from booking to handover.
summary: MoreSpace connects property portals, WhatsApp, your CRM, ERP and site teams so every enquiry gets a fast, consented reply, visits and bookings run on schedule, buyers see progress and dues clearly, and sites report every day. AI drafts, sorts and summarizes; your sales, legal, finance and site leads decide.
shareText: How MoreSpace automates real estate: instant portal lead replies, site visits, bookings, demand letters, snag lists, lease renewals and daily site reports, with your people approving every decision.
audience: Managing directors, sales heads and CRM heads at residential developers
Channel partner managers, brokerage owners and NRI desk leads
Leasing and asset managers at commercial landlords and co-working operators
Owners, project managers and safety officers at construction firms
Marketing heads managing portal, Meta and Google lead spend
Finance controllers and legal teams handling bookings, demands and agreements

challenges.title: Portal and ad leads go cold within minutes
challenges.description: Enquiries from 99acres, MagicBricks, Housing.com, Meta and Google arrive around the clock into separate dashboards and inboxes. The same buyer appears from several sources, nobody owns the first call, and by the time someone rings back the buyer has already spoken to another project.

challenges.title: Channel partner claims turn into disputes
challenges.description: Brokers register the same customer, direct enquirers walk in after a partner's visit, and brokerage depends on spreadsheets and memory. Each dispute costs partner trust and delays payouts, and partners hold back their best clients.

challenges.title: Bookings, demands and loans run on paper chases
challenges.description: KYC copies, allotment letters, agreement drafts, bank sanctions and milestone demand letters move between sales, CRM, legal, finance and lender relationship managers by email and paper. An error in a demand letter or a missed disbursement request hurts both cash flow and buyer confidence.

challenges.title: Buyers feel in the dark until possession
challenges.description: Progress updates are irregular and do not always match what the developer files with the RERA authority. Possession appointments, final dues questions and snag complaints are handled on calls, and defect reports after handover go missing.

challenges.title: Site information arrives late and in pieces
challenges.description: Daily progress sits in WhatsApp groups, labor counts on paper and material requests in phone calls. Project managers and clients see slippage days late, subcontractor bills cannot be checked against attendance, and near misses are never recorded.

challenges.title: Regulation touches every message and site
challenges.description: RERA details in every advertisement, DPDP consent and security duties, TRAI rules for calls and SMS, PMLA duties for larger brokerages and labor code obligations on site all apply at once. Personal phones and spreadsheets cannot show what was sent, approved or consented to.

flagship.title: Every enquiry answered, qualified and walked to a site visit
flagship.summary: One lead engine connects portals, Meta and Google lead forms, the website, missed-call numbers and channel partner registrations to your CRM. Each enquiry is deduplicated and attributed, answered within minutes with approved project content and the RERA registration number, qualified, assigned with response-time alerts and taken through visit booking, reminders, gallery check-in and follow-up.

steps.title: Capture and deduplicate every source
steps.description: Portal pushes or pulls, ad lead forms, website forms, missed calls and partner registrations reach the CRM within seconds and are matched by phone, email and portal lead ID, so each buyer has one record with every source kept for attribution.

steps.title: Reply within minutes, with consent
steps.description: Opted-in leads receive an approved WhatsApp template with the brochure, RERA registration number and next steps; others get a prompt call from the assigned executive, who offers the opt-in. Questions are answered only from the approved project knowledge base.

steps.title: Qualify and assign with alerts
steps.description: A short WhatsApp Flow or call script records configuration, budget band, timeline, home-loan need and resident or NRI status. Rules set by the sales head score and assign the lead, and the sales manager is alerted when contact slips past the agreed window.

steps.title: Book and confirm the site visit
steps.description: Buyers pick a gallery slot on WhatsApp, receive reminders with the location pin and reschedule buttons, and check in by QR code on arrival, which also confirms any channel partner attribution.

steps.title: Follow up and learn
steps.description: The executive confirms an AI summary of the visit, selected follow-up content goes out, and dashboards show response time, visit show-up and visit-to-booking conversion by source, campaign, partner and executive.

flagship.humanCheckpoint: Sales executives own every qualified conversation and every price, offer or possession-date answer, using the approved price sheet. The sales manager reviews response breaches daily, the partner manager decides attribution conflicts, and marketing and legal approve templates, ad copy and RERA details before launch.
outcomes: Faster first contact on portal and ad leads, including evenings and weekends
Fewer duplicate leads and attribution disputes between sources and partners
More visits kept, because confirming or rescheduling takes one tap
Clear evidence of which sources, campaigns and partners produce visits and bookings

stages.title: Discover and enquire
stages.description: Buyers, tenants, members and project owners find a project, space or builder through portals, ads, partners, hoardings, referrals and tenders, and expect a useful reply within minutes, often on WhatsApp and often after office hours.
touchpoints: Property portals such as 99acres, MagicBricks and Housing.com
Meta and Google lead forms and the website
Hoardings, site boards and missed-call numbers
stages.owner: Pre-sales head, channel partner manager or bid manager

stages.title: Visit and evaluate
stages.description: Prospects see the site, sample flat or center in person or by video, compare options and costs, and bring family members, partners or brokers into the decision.
touchpoints: Video site visits for buyers abroad
stages.owner: Sales manager, NRI desk lead or center manager

stages.title: Book, document and finance
stages.description: The buyer or occupier commits: booking amount, KYC, allotment letter, agreement for sale and its registration, home-loan sanction, lease or membership signing, and brokerage for the partner who introduced them.
stages.owner: CRM head, legal team and finance controller

stages.title: Build and pay
stages.description: Construction moves through certified stages while buyers pay milestone demands, lenders disburse, and site teams manage progress, labor, materials and safety every day.
touchpoints: Daily site reports and material requests
stages.owner: Project head with the finance controller

stages.title: Possession and move-in
stages.description: Once the occupancy certificate or fit-out completion is in hand, buyers and tenants clear final dues, inspect the space, raise snags and take possession or move in.
touchpoints: Possession offer and final dues statement
stages.owner: CRM handover manager and quality engineer

stages.title: Occupy, renew and refer
stages.description: Owners and tenants live with the space: rent and escalations, renewals and exits, maintenance and defect reports, and referrals to friends and colleagues.
stages.owner: Asset manager, facility head or CRM head

segments.name: Residential developers
segments.headline: Turn portal enquiries into site visits, bookings and on-time collections
segments.summary: Developers juggle launches, inventory, channel partners, banks and buyers at different stages, all at once. We connect portals, WhatsApp, the CRM and the ERP so leads are answered fast, visits are confirmed, bookings move from KYC to registered agreement, demands follow certified milestones and possession runs from one snag list.
challenges: Launch weekends bring a flood of portal, ad and hoarding enquiries that pre-sales cannot call back fast enough, and attribution between sources and partners is unreliable.
Site visits are booked by phone, buyers forget or arrive at the wrong gallery, and what happened during the visit never reaches the CRM.
Demand letters are prepared in spreadsheets from the ERP, checked by hand and sent without the progress evidence that buyers and their lenders ask for.
Possession brings a rush of handover appointments, final dues queries and snag complaints tracked on calls and paper.

uses.title: Instant, consented lead response
uses.description: Portal, Meta, Google, website and missed-call leads deduplicated and answered in minutes with the brochure and RERA registration number, then qualified and assigned with response-time alerts.

uses.title: Site visits that actually happen
uses.description: WhatsApp visit booking against gallery capacity, reminders with the location pin, QR check-in that confirms partner attribution, and visit notes summarized into the CRM.

uses.title: NRI desk across time zones
uses.description: Replies and updates in the buyer's own daytime, video site visits, and answers on eligibility and NRE, NRO or FCNR payments drawn only from an FAQ your legal team approves.

uses.title: Booking desk on one record
uses.description: Secure KYC links, allotment letters and agreement drafts from legal-approved templates, registration appointments, a control on advances before the registered agreement, and home-loan cases tracked by lender.

uses.title: Milestone demands with evidence
uses.description: Demand letters released only after the architect's or engineer's certificate and finance approval, sent with photos of the completed stage and disbursement request packs for lenders.

uses.title: Possession and snag control
uses.description: Handover slots, final dues statements, room-by-room snag reporting with photos, contractor assignment with verified closure, and defect tickets that stay open after handover.

systems: Real estate CRM such as Sell.Do, LeadSquared or Salesforce
ERP such as Farvision or SAP for inventory and receivables
State RERA portal and project page

segments.name: Brokers & channel partners
segments.headline: Register clients first, close faster and get paid on time
segments.summary: Brokers and channel partners win on speed and trust: replying first, protecting their client registrations and getting brokerage paid without chasing. We give brokerages and the developers they work with a shared, auditable record from registration to payout, plus KYC and record-keeping built for PMLA duties where they apply.
challenges: The same client is registered by several partners or walks in directly, and without timestamps nobody can show who introduced them first.
Listing and portal enquiries land on agents' personal phones, so follow-up depends on each agent's memory and leaves with the agent.
Brokerage waits on booking milestones, developer approvals and invoice corrections, and partners cannot see where a payout stands.
Brokerages above the PMLA turnover threshold must verify clients, keep records and report suspicious transactions, which personal chats and email cannot support.

uses.title: Client registration with proof
uses.description: Registrations by portal or WhatsApp form, checked against existing leads and other partners, timestamped and confirmed with a reference number and validity period.

uses.title: One inbox for every enquiry
uses.description: Portal listing and social enquiries routed to the right agent with an instant approved reply, short qualification and follow-up reminders, instead of scattered personal phones.

uses.title: Visits coordinated with developers
uses.description: Client visits booked against developer gallery slots, with a QR check-in that links the visit to your registration and alerts you on arrival.

uses.title: NRI client service
uses.description: Time-zone aware follow-up and video site visits for clients abroad, with eligibility and payment answers drawn only from approved content.

uses.title: PMLA-ready KYC files
uses.description: Secure KYC collection, screening against the lists your AML policy names, five-year records with an access log, and a private review queue for your Principal Officer.

uses.title: Brokerage you can track
uses.description: Deals by developer and milestone, statements, invoices, payments received and agent splits, with reminders when a developer payment runs past the agreed period.

kpis: KYC files complete before token payment
systems: FIU-IND FINGate portal for reporting entities
Accounting such as Tally for GST invoices

segments.name: Commercial leasing & co-working
segments.headline: Fill space faster and stay ahead of every rent, escalation and renewal date
segments.summary: Office landlords and co-working operators sell space on two clocks: fast tours and proposals for new occupiers, and long lease calendars for existing ones. We connect enquiries, center calendars, proposals, leases and billing so tours convert, handovers are tracked and every rent, escalation and renewal date reaches the right person in time.
challenges: Requirements arrive from property consultants, aggregators, Google and walk-ins in different formats, and availability lives in a spreadsheet that is rarely current.
Tours are arranged by phone across centers, and proposals take days because pricing exceptions are approved over email.
Escalation, lock-in and renewal notice dates sit inside signed lease PDFs, so they surface only when a tenant serves notice.
Fit-out handovers and snag items for new tenants are tracked in WhatsApp groups between leasing, projects and facilities.

uses.title: Requirement matching
uses.description: Enquiries for desks, cabins or floors matched to live inventory from the co-working platform or stacking plan, with consultant or aggregator attribution recorded.

uses.title: Tours across centers
uses.description: Tour slots by center and manager, confirmations and reminders on WhatsApp, and day passes where your operating model offers them.

uses.title: Proposals within the price book
uses.description: Proposals generated from approved pricing and discount bands, with exceptions routed to the center head or leasing director before they reach the client.

uses.title: Onboarding from one record
uses.description: Company KYC, e-signature, access cards, Wi-Fi and billing set up from the signed agreement, so new members are not waiting on separate teams.

uses.title: A lease calendar you can trust
uses.description: Abstracts extracted from signed leases and verified by the leasing manager drive rent, escalation, lock-in and renewal reminders, with brokerage on new leases tracked to payout.

uses.title: Fit-out handover and snags
uses.description: Warm-shell or fitted-out handovers with snag lists, contractor assignment and verified closure before the tenant moves in.

systems: Lease management such as Yardi or MRI Software
Co-working platforms such as Nexudus or OfficeRnD
Accounting and GST invoicing such as Tally or SAP

segments.name: Construction & contracting
segments.headline: See every site, every day: bids, progress, labor, materials and safety
segments.summary: Contractors run on thin margins and late information. We turn RFQs and BOQs into a tracked bid pipeline and give site engineers one daily report for progress, labor and material requests, with approvals by value, serious safety events escalated at once and snags closed with photo evidence for the client.
challenges: RFQs arrive as emails with PDF BOQs and drawings, estimators retype line items, and clarification deadlines are tracked in personal inboxes.
Progress, manpower and material use come from WhatsApp groups and paper registers, so the project manager sees the true position days late.
Material requests go by phone and are approved without a check against BOQ balance or site stock, so sites over-order or stop work for a missing item.
Near misses go unreported, serious incidents are relayed by phone with details lost, and statutory notices and registers depend on one person's memory.

uses.title: Bid desk
uses.description: RFQ register, BOQ extraction mapped to your rate library, vendor quote requests and deadline reminders, with the estimator approving every rate.

uses.title: One daily site report
uses.description: Progress against plan, photos, manpower by subcontractor, equipment, materials received and hindrances in one mobile form that works offline and syncs later.

uses.title: Labor attendance reconciliation
uses.description: Headcount from biometric or app-based attendance matched against reported manpower, so subcontractor bills can be checked against who was actually on site.

uses.title: Material requests with approvals
uses.description: Requests checked against BOQ balance, drawing revision and site stock, routed by value, ordered by purchase and received with challan photos.

uses.title: Safety incident and near-miss log
uses.description: QR and WhatsApp reporting in the languages used on site, immediate phone escalation for serious events, investigations, corrective actions and draft statutory notices.

uses.title: Snag rectification for clients
uses.description: Snags from the developer's or tenant's handover assigned to your trades with due dates, closed with after photos and verified by the client's quality engineer.

kpis: Win rate by client and work type
systems: Scheduling in Primavera P6 or Microsoft Project
Site apps such as Powerplay or Procore
ERP such as SAP or Tally for purchase and stock
Government e-procurement portals such as CPPP or GeM

automations.title: Portal and ad lead capture with instant response and qualification
automations.summary: Enquiries from property portals, Meta and Google lead forms, the website and missed-call numbers reach one CRM queue within seconds, are deduplicated and answered with approved project content, then qualified and assigned to an executive with response-time alerts.
automations.problem: Portal and ad leads arrive at all hours into separate dashboards and inboxes. The same buyer enquires on several portals, nobody owns the first call, and slow follow-up wastes media spend. Generic chatbots, meanwhile, risk quoting the wrong price or promising a possession date.
automations.trigger: A lead arrives through a portal push or pull integration (99acres, MagicBricks or Housing.com, for example), a Meta or Google lead form, the website, a missed-call number or a QR code on a hoarding.
steps: Normalize the phone number and project, match the lead against CRM records by phone, email and portal lead ID, and merge duplicates while keeping every source for attribution.

Read the consent captured by the source form: opted-in leads get an approved WhatsApp template with the brochure, RERA registration number and next steps; others get a call from the assigned executive, who offers the opt-in.
Collect configuration, budget band, preferred location, purchase timeline, home-loan need and resident or NRI status through a short WhatsApp Flow or the executive's call script.

Answer questions on amenities, location, carpet area and price range only from the approved project knowledge base, citing the entry used; offers, discounts and possession dates are handed to the executive.
Score the lead against rules the sales head sets, assign it by project, language or round robin, and alert the sales manager when no meaningful contact happens within the agreed window.
Report response time, qualification and cost per qualified lead by source, campaign and portal package every week.
automations.humanCheckpoint: The assigned executive owns every qualified conversation and makes the first call where there is no WhatsApp opt-in. Prices come only from the approved price sheet; offers, discounts, payment-plan changes and possession dates go to the executive or sales manager. Marketing and legal approve all templates.
systems: Portal lead feeds such as 99acres, MagicBricks and Housing.com
Real estate CRM such as Sell.Do, LeadSquared or Salesforce
Approved price sheet and project brochure
automations.data: Uses name, phone, email, project and qualification answers only; no identity documents at this stage. The consent source, notice version and WhatsApp opt-in are stored with the lead, and STOP or a do-not-contact request ends outreach on every channel. Unconverted leads are deleted or anonymized after the retention period the client sets. Model calls run under terms that exclude training on the data.
kpis: Speed to first contact by source
Leads contacted within the agreed window
outputs: Portal, ad and website lead integrations with duplicate rules
Approved WhatsApp templates and qualification Flow
Project knowledge base with named content owners

automations.title: Channel partner client registration with duplicate and conflict checks
automations.summary: Partners register clients through a simple portal or WhatsApp form before a visit. Each registration is checked against existing leads and other partners, timestamped, confirmed with a validity period and linked to the visit, so attribution rests on evidence rather than memory.
automations.problem: When two partners claim the same buyer, or a buyer who enquired directly arrives with a broker, the decision depends on screenshots and phone calls. Disputes sour partner relationships, delay brokerage and make partners reluctant to bring their best clients to the developer.
automations.trigger: An empanelled partner submits a client registration for a project through the partner portal or a WhatsApp Flow, or arrives at the sales gallery with a client who is not yet registered.
steps: Confirm the partner is empanelled for the project and that the RERA agent registration number on file is present and valid, and pause new registrations from partners whose registration has lapsed.
Normalize the client's phone and name, and record the partner's confirmation that the client agreed to share their details with the developer.
Check the client against direct leads, other partners' registrations and past bookings within the validity window set in the developer's written partner policy.

Confirm a clean registration to the partner with a reference number and expiry date; send possible duplicates to the partner manager with a timeline of every touch, without revealing other parties' details.
At the gallery, a QR check-in links the visit to the registration and alerts the partner; registrations near expiry prompt the partner to book a visit or renew under the policy.
Log every decision with its evidence for the brokerage stage and for monthly partner reviews.
automations.humanCheckpoint: The channel partner manager decides every flagged duplicate or conflict under the written partner policy, and the sales head hears appeals. The automation never rejects a disputed claim on its own, and partners see only their own registrations.
systems: Developer CRM such as Sell.Do or Salesforce
automations.data: Holds the client's name, phone and project, plus the partner's identity, RERA agent number and empanelment status. Partners see only their own clients, and a duplicate check reveals that a match exists, never another party's details. Registration and decision logs are kept for the brokerage and dispute period the policy sets, and processing logs for at least one year.
kpis: Registrations blocked for lapsed RERA agent numbers
outputs: Partner registration portal and WhatsApp Flow
Duplicate and validity rules written from the partner policy
Conflict queue with an evidence timeline
Gallery QR check-in linked to registrations

automations.title: RFQ and BOQ intake with extraction, vendor quotes and bid tracking
automations.summary: Tender and RFQ emails become entries in a bid register. AI extracts BOQ line items from spreadsheets and PDFs into a structured sheet mapped to your rate library and flags missing specifications, and the team tracks quotes, clarifications and deadlines until the estimator signs off.
automations.problem: Estimators spend days retyping BOQs from PDFs and spreadsheets, vendor quotes come back late or not at all, and pre-bid and clarification deadlines are tracked in personal inboxes. Good tenders are missed and rushed bids carry pricing errors.
automations.trigger: An RFQ, tender notice or addendum arrives in the bids mailbox or is downloaded from a client or government e-procurement portal, with drawings, specifications and a BOQ.
steps: Create a bid record with client, scope, pre-bid and submission dates, earnest money and document list, and post a summary to the bid channel for a go or no-go decision.
Extract BOQ items, units and quantities from spreadsheets or PDFs into a structured sheet, keeping the original item numbers and page references.
Suggest matching codes from the contractor's rate library, and flag items with no match, unclear specifications or unusual quantities for the estimator.
Send quote requests for unmatched materials and subcontract packages to approved vendors, and chase replies before the internal cut-off.
Track pre-bid queries, client clarifications and addenda against the affected BOQ items, and remind owners of every deadline.
Record submission, opening results, published competitor rates and the win or loss reason for use in future bids.
automations.humanCheckpoint: The chief estimator reviews every extracted line against the source document and approves every rate; extraction stays a draft until checked. A director approves the go or no-go decision, the margin and the final submission.
systems: Government e-procurement portals such as CPPP or GeM
ERP such as SAP or Tally for the vendor master
automations.data: Works on tender documents, drawings and vendor quotes, which are commercially confidential: they stay in the contractor's own workspace with access limited to the bid team. Client documents are used only for the bid in question, and model calls run under terms that exclude training on the data. Vendor contacts come from the approved vendor master.
kpis: Win rate by client and work type
outputs: Bid register with deadlines and owners
BOQ extraction workflow with a review screen

automations.title: Site visit booking, reminders, check-in and post-visit follow-up
automations.summary: Qualified buyers book a site visit on WhatsApp against sales gallery capacity, receive reminders with the location pin, check in by QR code on arrival and get a feedback request afterwards, while the executive's notes become a confirmed CRM summary and next step.
automations.problem: Visits are booked over the phone and forgotten, buyers arrive at the wrong gallery or at the busiest hour, and what happened during the visit lives in the executive's head. Interested buyers cool off because nobody follows up with the right unit, floor plan or cost sheet at the right time.
automations.trigger: A qualified lead accepts a visit in the WhatsApp Flow, an executive books one in the CRM, or a channel partner books one for a registered client.
steps: Offer visit slots by project and gallery based on executive rosters and weekend capacity, and write the booking to the CRM against the lead and any partner registration.
Confirm with an approved template carrying the location pin, parking and what to bring, then send reminders the day before and a few hours before with reschedule and cancel buttons.
On arrival, a QR check-in at the gallery records the visit, alerts the assigned executive and confirms attribution for any registered partner.
After the visit, the executive dictates or types notes; AI drafts a summary of units shown, objections and next step, which the executive confirms before it is saved.
Send a short feedback request and the follow-up content the executive selected, such as the floor plan or cost sheet, and schedule the agreed callback.
Show no-shows, revisits and visit-to-booking conversion by project, source, partner and executive.
automations.humanCheckpoint: Executives confirm every AI visit summary before it enters the CRM and choose what follow-up content is sent. Cost sheets are generated only from the approved price sheet, and the sales manager reviews hot leads and any negotiation every day.
systems: Real estate CRM such as Sell.Do, LeadSquared or Salesforce
Approved price sheet and cost sheet templates
automations.data: Uses name, phone, project, slot and visit notes, and notes should not record personal details beyond what the sale needs. Reminders follow the buyer's WhatsApp opt-in, and the buyer can stop messages at any time. Visit records stay in the CRM under the client's retention policy, with access limited to the sales team for that project.
kpis: Time from visit to next contact
outputs: WhatsApp visit booking Flow and approved templates
AI visit summary with executive confirmation
Visit funnel dashboard by project, source and partner

automations.title: NRI buyer nurturing across time zones with video site visits
automations.summary: Buyers abroad get replies and updates in their own daytime, book video site visits that overlap with Indian working hours, and receive answers on eligibility, payments and documentation only from content your legal team approves, with an NRI desk manager owning every relationship.
automations.problem: NRI enquiries arrive overnight Indian time and wait until morning, and follow-ups land in the middle of the buyer's night. Questions about NRE or NRO payments, power of attorney and repatriation get informal, inconsistent answers from different executives, and family members in India are left out of the conversation.
automations.trigger: A lead is identified as living abroad by its country code, a form answer or the executive's tag in the CRM.
steps: Record the buyer's country, time zone and preferred contact hours, and collect a WhatsApp and email opt-in that names the developer.
Schedule replies, reminders and updates inside the buyer's local daytime, with a live handover to the NRI desk during overlapping hours.
Offer a video site visit with an executive at the project, and invite a family member the buyer nominates in India to a physical visit if the buyer wishes.

Answer questions on eligibility, payment through NRE, NRO or FCNR accounts or inward remittance, power of attorney and documents only from the FAQ legal approves; tax and individual cases go to the legal team or the buyer's adviser.
Send a monthly email digest of construction progress and new releases to opted-in buyers, with an unsubscribe link in every email.
Track responses, video visits and bookings by country and source.
automations.humanCheckpoint: The NRI desk relationship manager owns each buyer and handles every pricing, booking and documentation conversation. Legal approves the FAQ and the power of attorney guidance, and no automated message gives tax or foreign exchange advice on an individual case.
systems: Legal-approved NRI FAQ and document checklist
automations.data: Uses name, contact details, country, time zone and preferences; passport and address proofs are collected only at booking. Where buyers live in the EU or UK, the GDPR or UK GDPR may also apply, so consent, transfer and retention terms are reviewed in discovery. Email and WhatsApp opt-outs are honored on every channel, and inactive records are deleted after the agreed period.
kpis: Response time in the buyer's local hours

automations.title: Office and co-working enquiries from tour to signed agreement
automations.summary: Enquiries for desks, cabins or office floors are qualified, matched to live inventory, booked into a center tour and followed by a proposal from the approved price book. New members and tenants are onboarded with company KYC, access and billing set up from one record.
automations.problem: Requirements arrive from consultants, aggregators, Google and walk-ins, and availability lives in a spreadsheet that is rarely current. Tours are arranged over calls across centers, proposals wait for pricing approval by email, and new members wait days for access cards and invoices.
automations.trigger: An enquiry arrives from the website, Google Business Profile, an aggregator or broker, a WhatsApp message, or a walk-in logged by the community manager.
steps: Capture seats or area, move-in date, term, budget and location, and attribute the enquiry to the consultant, broker or aggregator where one is involved.
Match the requirement to live inventory from the co-working platform or the landlord's stacking plan, and shortlist suitable options.
Book a tour with the center or leasing manager, send confirmations and reminders, and offer a day pass where the operator allows it.
Generate a proposal from the approved price book within the discount band, with exceptions routed to the center head or leasing director.
On acceptance, collect company KYC such as GSTIN and authorized signatory, send the membership agreement or letter of intent for e-signature, and set up access, Wi-Fi and billing.
Report enquiry-to-tour time, tour-to-signing conversion, occupancy and lost-deal reasons by center and channel.
automations.humanCheckpoint: Community and leasing managers run every tour and negotiation. Discounts outside the approved band need the center head, and lease terms, letters of intent and enterprise agreements are approved by the leasing director and legal before signature.
systems: Co-working platform such as Nexudus or OfficeRnD
automations.data: Uses business contact details, company name, GSTIN and signatory identity. KYC documents sit in restricted storage visible only to the onboarding and finance team, and broker details are kept for brokerage. Enquiries that do not convert are deleted after the period the operator sets.
outputs: Proposal generator tied to the price book
Onboarding checklist covering KYC, access and billing

automations.title: Booking to registered agreement: KYC, allotment and home loans
automations.summary: After a booking, buyers complete a secure application with KYC, the CRM team verifies it, allotment letters and agreement drafts come from legal-approved templates, demands stay within the RERA advance limit until registration, and each home-loan case is tracked with the buyer's lender.
automations.problem: Booking forms, KYC copies, payment proofs, allotment letters and agreement drafts move between sales, CRM, legal, finance and lenders by email and paper. Missing documents delay registration, demands can exceed the advance RERA allows before a registered agreement, and buyers cannot tell where their loan or paperwork stands.
automations.trigger: A sales executive marks a unit as booked in the CRM or ERP and the booking amount is received through the bank or payment gateway.
steps: Send the buyer a secure, expiring link to complete the application for every applicant, upload PAN and address proof, or passport and visa details for NRIs, and confirm the unit, price and payment plan.
Match the booking amount against bank or gateway records, and block any further demand above the advance RERA permits until the agreement for sale is registered.
Queue the file for CRM verification; once verified, generate the allotment letter from the legal-approved template and send it for authorized signature.

If the buyer needs a loan, record their consent to share status with the lender they choose, send that lender's checklist and the list of banks that have approved the project, and track sanction and any tripartite agreement.
Prepare the agreement for sale from the state's prescribed format for legal review, book the registration appointment, and track stamp duty and registration fees.
Keep the buyer informed at each step with approved WhatsApp and email updates, and show every file's status and blocker on a CRM team board.
automations.humanCheckpoint: The CRM team verifies every KYC file and legal approves every allotment letter and agreement. Any deviation in price, payment plan or terms needs the sales head and finance controller. Lenders decide loans, and nothing is shared with a lender without the buyer's consent.
systems: ERP such as Farvision or SAP for units and receivables
State registration portal for appointments and fees
automations.data: KYC documents are stored encrypted in the developer's own storage with Aadhaar numbers masked, and only the CRM and legal team can open them. Income documents go from the buyer directly to the lender; the tracker holds loan status, sanction amount and dates only. Records are kept for the period the agreement, tax and registration rules require.
outputs: Secure buyer application and KYC upload
Booking file board with blockers and owners
Advance-limit control before the registered agreement

automations.title: Client KYC and PMLA record-keeping for brokerages
automations.summary: As a deal moves toward closure, the brokerage collects client KYC through a secure link, records beneficial ownership and payment details, screens names against the lists its AML policy requires and keeps a five-year record. Possible red flags go privately to the Principal Officer.
automations.problem: Brokerages above the PMLA turnover threshold are reporting entities, yet client documents often sit in agents' phones and email. Without a consistent file, the firm cannot show due diligence, retrieve records for the required period or route a concern to the Principal Officer without alerting the client.
automations.trigger: An agent marks a deal as agreed in principle, or a client is about to pay a token or booking amount on a sale or purchase the brokerage facilitates.
steps: Send the client, and the other party where the brokerage acts for both, a secure link to upload identity and address documents and, for companies or trusts, beneficial ownership details.
Verify documents through an approved verification service where the client consents, and record the method and result.
Screen names against the sanctions and other lists the brokerage's AML policy requires, including the UN sanctions list, and hold the file on a possible match.
Record payment mode, paying party and a source-of-funds declaration, and flag the patterns the policy defines, such as large cash components, third-party payers or unexplained structures.
Send flags only to the Principal Officer's private queue with the evidence; the agent sees that the file is on hold, not why.
Keep KYC and transaction records for five years under the record-keeping rules, with an access log and a search for inspections.
automations.humanCheckpoint: The Principal Officer reviews every flag and decides whether a report is required; the automation never files with FIU-IND and never contacts the client about a flag. The Designated Director approves the AML policy and screening lists, and the brokerage's legal advisers confirm thresholds and duties.
systems: Sanctions and watch lists named in the AML policy
FIU-IND FINGate portal, used by the Principal Officer
automations.data: Identity documents are encrypted, Aadhaar numbers masked, and access limited to the compliance team and the deal's agent. Flag details are visible only to the Principal Officer and Designated Director, which supports the rule against tipping off. Records are kept for five years, then deleted unless another law or an open matter requires longer.
kpis: KYC files complete before token payment
Time from flag to Principal Officer decision
outputs: Secure KYC collection and verification flow
Screening and red-flag rules taken from the AML policy
Five-year record store with an access log

automations.title: Brokerage eligibility, invoicing and payout tracking
automations.summary: Every deal's brokerage terms, milestones, invoices and payments sit on one record. Developers and landlords see which partner claims are due and approve them; brokerages see what each developer owes them and how commissions split among their agents.
automations.problem: Brokerage depends on booking milestones, agreement registration, payment receipts and slab terms that differ by project and period. Partners send invoices that do not match, finance cannot see what is due, and payouts stall while partners chase sales teams on WhatsApp.
automations.trigger: A booking or lease reaches the brokerage milestone in the partner agreement, such as agreement registration and receipt of the agreed payment, or the start of a lease.
steps: Read the deal, milestone status and receipts from the CRM, ERP or lease system, and calculate eligible brokerage from the partner agreement and the project's slab rules.
Publish a brokerage statement to the partner portal and invite an invoice, with GSTIN and bank details checked against the empanelment record.
Compare the invoice with the statement, send mismatches back to the partner, and route matched invoices for sales or leasing head and finance approval.
Post approved payouts to the accounting system, with tax deductions applied by finance, and notify the partner when payment is released.
Flag cancellations and refunds that trigger a clawback or adjustment under the agreement, for finance to decide.
For brokerages, track receivables by developer and agent splits, and remind owners of invoices unpaid beyond the agreed period.
automations.humanCheckpoint: The finance controller approves every payout and every clawback, and the sales or leasing head approves any slab exception. The automation calculates, checks and reminds; it never releases money.
systems: Developer CRM or ERP booking records
Lease management system for commercial deals
Accounting such as Tally or SAP
automations.data: Uses deal value, milestones, partner PAN, GSTIN and bank details. Bank and tax details are visible to finance only, and partners see only their own deals. Statements, approvals and payment references are kept for the period tax and accounting rules require.
outputs: Brokerage rules taken from partner agreements
Approval workflow with an audit trail

automations.title: Construction progress updates and milestone-linked demand letters
automations.summary: When the project's architect or engineer certifies a construction stage, buyers receive a progress update with photos and a demand letter calculated from their payment plan, once finance approves the batch. Lenders get disbursement requests for loan buyers, and monthly updates fill the gaps.
automations.problem: Demand letters are compiled from the ERP in spreadsheets, checked by hand and sent without evidence that the stage is complete. Buyers and lenders push back, disbursements arrive late and collections slip. Progress updates are irregular and sometimes disagree with what the developer files on the RERA portal.
automations.trigger: A construction stage in the payment plan, such as a slab or masonry milestone, is certified by the project's architect or engineer and approved by the project head in the ERP, or the monthly update date arrives.
steps: Collect the stage certificate, site photos and tower-wise progress from the site team's reports, and draft a plain-language update from those facts only.
Route the update to the project head and marketing for approval, checking stated progress against the figures in the latest RERA quarterly update.
Generate demand letters per unit from the payment plan with amount, taxes, due date and the project's designated collection account, and run a maker-checker review of totals and a sample of letters.
Release the approved batch by email with the letter and update, plus a WhatsApp notification with a secure link, and send lenders the disbursement request pack for loan buyers.

Remind buyers before the due date, match receipts from bank statements, and pass overdue cases to the CRM team with history; any interest under the agreement is calculated for finance to review, never applied automatically.
Show demanded, collected and overdue amounts by tower and milestone, and disbursement requests pending with each lender.
automations.humanCheckpoint: No demand goes out without the architect's or engineer's certificate, the project head's approval and the finance controller's batch approval. Interest, waivers and payment-plan changes are decided by finance and the CRM head, and the project head approves every progress statement.
systems: ERP such as Farvision or SAP for payment plans and receivables
Bank statements for the designated collection account
automations.data: Uses unit, buyer contact, payment plan, amounts and loan status. Letters are delivered behind expiring links, never as open attachments in group chats. Financial records stay in the ERP, and delivery and approval logs are kept for the agreement's term and at least one year. AI drafting uses project progress data only, never buyer data.
outputs: Progress update drafting and approval flow
Collections dashboard by tower and milestone

automations.title: Daily site reports, labor attendance and material approvals
automations.summary: Site engineers file one mobile daily report covering work done against plan, photos, manpower by subcontractor, equipment, materials received and material requests. Attendance is reconciled, requests are checked against BOQ balance and routed by value, and managers get a daily digest.
automations.problem: Progress, labor counts and material needs arrive as WhatsApp photos, calls and paper registers. Project managers see slippage days late, subcontractor bills cannot be checked against actual manpower, and materials are ordered without checking BOQ balance or site stock.
automations.trigger: The site engineer opens the daily report before the end of the shift, or raises a material request between reports.
steps: Collect activities and quantities against the planned schedule, location-tagged photos, manpower by trade and subcontractor, equipment hours, materials received with challan photos, and hindrances, in a mobile form that also works offline.
Pull headcount from biometric or app-based attendance and flag gaps against the manpower reported for each subcontractor.
Check each material request against the BOQ balance, the current drawing revision and site stock, and flag requests above balance for the quantity surveyor.
Route requests for approval by value, from site in-charge to project manager to purchase head, with purchase raising the order in the ERP.
Compare reported progress with the schedule baseline, and send the project manager a daily digest of slippage, idle labor, stock risks and open issues.
Compile a weekly progress report with photos for the client or developer, reviewed by the project manager before it is shared.
automations.humanCheckpoint: The project manager reviews the daily digest and approves material requests within their limit; the purchase head approves higher values and the quantity surveyor approves anything above BOQ balance. Subcontractor bills are certified by the project manager and accounts, not by the automation.
systems: Schedule in Primavera P6 or Microsoft Project
Site apps such as Powerplay or Procore
ERP such as SAP or Tally for purchase orders and stock
automations.data: Worker data is limited to name, ID, trade, subcontractor and attendance times; biometric templates stay in the attendance device or vendor system and are never copied. Photos show work, not faces, wherever possible. Attendance and wage-related records are kept for the periods labor rules require, with access limited to site administration and HR.
kpis: Manpower variance between attendance and reports
outputs: Material request approval matrix with BOQ checks
Daily digest and weekly client report

automations.title: Safety incident and near-miss logging with immediate escalation
automations.summary: Anyone on site can report an injury, dangerous occurrence or near miss by WhatsApp or QR code, with photos. Serious events trigger immediate calls to the safety officer and project head, corrective actions are tracked, and statutory notices are drafted for the responsible person to file.
automations.problem: Near misses go unreported, serious incidents are relayed by phone with details lost, and the statutory notices and registers that labor law requires depend on one person remembering the deadlines. Corrective actions from one site rarely reach the next.
automations.trigger: A worker, supervisor or engineer scans the site safety QR code or messages the site safety number, or a toolbox talk or inspection records an unsafe condition.
steps: Capture what happened, where, who was involved, any injuries, photos and immediate actions in a short form offered in the languages used on site.

Classify severity using the safety officer's rules; fatal accidents, serious injuries and dangerous occurrences such as a scaffold or structure collapse trigger immediate calls and messages to the safety officer, site in-charge and project head.
Open an investigation record with timeline, witnesses, root-cause fields and corrective actions with owners and due dates.
Draft statutory notices and register entries from the record for the safety officer to complete and file within the deadlines the applicable rules set.
Track corrective actions to closure with photo evidence, and share lessons across sites in a weekly safety bulletin.
Report incidents, near misses, open actions and toolbox talk coverage by site and subcontractor.
automations.humanCheckpoint: The site safety officer owns every report and decides severity, investigation and closure; first aid, medical care and emergency response never wait for the automation. The safety officer or employer files statutory notices, and the system only drafts and reminds. The project head reviews serious incidents that day.
systems: Site safety registers and permit-to-work records
State labor department portal for notices
automations.data: Holds the worker's name, ID, injury description and photos, which are sensitive: access is limited to the safety officer, site head and HR, and photos record conditions rather than faces. Records are kept for the period the applicable labor rules and the contractor's insurer require, and reporters can stay anonymous for near misses.
kpis: Time from report to safety officer acknowledgement
Corrective actions closed by due date
outputs: Multilingual incident and near-miss reporting flow
Severity rules and escalation call tree

automations.title: Possession, fit-out handover and snag-list management
automations.summary: After the occupancy certificate or fit-out completion, buyers and tenants book handover slots, receive a final dues statement, report snags room by room with photos and track each item as the contractor fixes it and a quality engineer verifies it. Later defect reports follow the same path.
automations.problem: Possession arrives in a rush: buyers call for dates and final dues, snag lists are written on paper during the walkthrough, and contractors receive them days later on WhatsApp. Items are closed without proof and reopened by unhappy buyers, and defect complaints after handover get lost although the developer remains responsible for years.
automations.trigger: The occupancy certificate is received and possession is offered for a tower, or a commercial floor's warm-shell or fit-out handover is ready; later, an owner or tenant reports a defect.
steps: Send the possession or handover offer with the final dues statement and document checklist, and offer handover slots by tower and floor.
During the pre-handover inspection, buyers or tenants log snags room by room with photos and a category, on a tablet with the handover executive or on their own phone.
Assign each snag to the responsible contractor or trade with a due date, and notify the contractor's site engineer.
Contractors close items with after photos, and the quality engineer verifies each closure before the buyer or tenant is asked to confirm.
Release keys or access once dues, documents and the agreed snags are complete, and record the handover acknowledgement.
Keep a defect reporting route open after handover, tracked as defect-liability tickets with the same assignment and verification steps.
automations.humanCheckpoint: The quality engineer verifies every closure and the CRM handover manager signs off each possession. Disputed snags, compensation questions and any structural concern go to the project head and, where needed, the structural consultant.
systems: ERP for final dues and possession status
Real estate CRM or lease system
automations.data: Uses unit, owner or tenant contact, dues status and snag photos of the property only. Contractors see the unit, location and snag, never buyer contact details. Handover and defect records are kept for at least the defect liability period, which RERA sets at five years from possession for units sold in registered projects.
outputs: Possession offer, dues and slot booking flow
Snag capture app with photo evidence

automations.title: Lease abstraction, rent, escalation and renewal reminders
automations.summary: Key dates and terms are extracted from signed leases and verified by the leasing manager. Rent invoices and reminders follow the lease calendar, escalations are calculated for finance to approve, and renewal and lock-in dates reach the asset manager early enough to act.
automations.problem: Escalation, lock-in, notice and renewal terms are buried in signed PDFs and a spreadsheet nobody fully trusts. Escalations are billed late or wrongly, receivables age without follow-up, and renewal talks start only when a tenant serves notice.
automations.trigger: A new lease or membership agreement is signed, or a calendar event arrives: rent due, escalation date, lock-in expiry, renewal notice window or security deposit review.
steps: Extract parties, area, rent, escalation clause, lock-in, notice period, renewal options, deposit and fit-out terms from the signed lease into a structured abstract with page references.
Hold each abstract until the leasing manager verifies every field against the lease, then load the dates into the lease calendar.
Trigger rent invoices with GST through accounts, send reminders before and after the due date, and pass overdue cases to the asset manager with history.
Calculate escalations from the clause and send the draft letter for finance approval before it reaches the tenant.
Alert the asset manager ahead of lock-in expiry and renewal notice windows with occupancy, payment history and open helpdesk tickets for that tenant.
Track renewal proposals and exits, including deposit reconciliation and the handback inspection.
automations.humanCheckpoint: The leasing manager verifies every abstract before any date is used. Finance approves escalation letters and invoices, legal approves notices, and the asset manager decides renewal terms and any rent concession.
systems: Lease management such as Yardi or MRI Software
Co-working platform such as Nexudus or OfficeRnD
Accounting such as Tally or SAP
automations.data: Uses lease terms, tenant company contacts and payment history. Leases stay in the landlord's document store, and extraction runs under terms that exclude training on the data. Access is limited to leasing, finance and legal, and abstracts and correspondence are kept for the lease term plus the period tax and contract records require.
outputs: Verified lease abstracts with page references
Rent and escalation workflow with finance approval

Schedules, BOQs, daily reports and material records for contractors and developer project teams, and the baseline against which reported progress is compared.
Leases, memberships, inventory, billing and access for commercial landlords and operators, and the source for lease calendars and occupancy.

kpis.name: Speed to first contact
kpis.definition: Median time from lead creation in any source to the first meaningful contact by automation or an executive, by source and for staffed and unstaffed hours.
kpis.why: Portal and ad leads compare several projects at once, and the first useful reply often wins the site visit.

kpis.name: Lead-to-site-visit conversion
kpis.definition: Share of qualified leads in a period that complete a site or video visit, by project, source, partner and executive.
kpis.why: Shows whether response, qualification and visit booking work together, and which sources deserve more spend.

kpis.name: Visit-to-booking conversion
kpis.definition: Share of completed visits that lead to a booking within an agreed window, from CRM records.
kpis.why: Measures the quality of visits and follow-up, not just their number.

kpis.name: Partner registration conflict rate
kpis.definition: Share of channel partner registrations flagged as duplicates or conflicts, with the median time to a recorded decision.
kpis.why: Few conflicts and quick decisions protect partner trust and keep brokerage moving.

kpis.name: Booking-to-agreement registration time
kpis.definition: Median days from booking to a registered agreement for sale, split into buyer document time, internal verification time and registration scheduling.
kpis.why: Separates delays the developer can fix from buyer and registration delays, and keeps advances within the RERA limit for longer files.

kpis.name: Demand-to-collection days
kpis.definition: Median days from demand letter release to receipt of the full amount, by tower, milestone and loan-funded or self-funded buyers.
kpis.why: The cash flow measure that milestone evidence, lender packs and reminders are meant to improve.

kpis.name: Snag closure time
kpis.definition: Median time from a snag being logged to verified closure, with the share reopened by the buyer or tenant.
kpis.why: Drives handover satisfaction and shows which contractors or trades need attention.

kpis.name: Daily report timeliness
kpis.definition: Share of site days with a complete daily report submitted before the agreed cut-off, by site and engineer.
kpis.why: Late or missing reports hide slippage, idle labor and material risks until they are expensive.

kpis.name: Renewals decided before notice deadline
kpis.definition: Share of leases and memberships reaching a recorded renewal or exit decision before the notice or lock-in date.
kpis.why: Late decisions turn into vacancy or rushed concessions.

kpis.name: Safety incident acknowledgement time
kpis.definition: Time from an incident or near-miss report to acknowledgement by the site safety officer, with the share of corrective actions closed by their due date.
kpis.why: Shows whether reports reach the accountable person quickly and lead to action.

governance: Approved sources only: automated answers come from approved price sheets, brochures, RERA project pages and FAQs with named owners; offers, possession dates and legal or tax questions always go to a person.
Consent and preferences first: every outreach is tied to a recorded consent source, WhatsApp opt-in or TRAI preference check, and STOP or do-not-call requests end outreach on every channel.

People approve money, contracts and safety: allotments, agreements, demand batches, interest, payouts, discounts, bid prices and escalations each have a named approver, and serious site incidents reach the safety officer by phone at once.
Least-privilege access: partners see only their own clients, contractors never see buyer contacts, KYC files are encrypted with Aadhaar numbers masked, and access is reviewed every quarter.

Logs and breach readiness: processing logs are kept for at least one year as the DPDP Rules require, and an incident runbook supports notice to affected people without delay and a detailed report to the Board within seventy-two hours.
Controlled change: templates, prompts and rules are versioned, tested against scripted edge cases and approved by their named owner before each release.

compliance.title: RERA: project and agent registration, and advertisements
compliance.description: Under the RERA Act 2016, a project that must register cannot be advertised, marketed, booked or sold before registration, every advertisement must prominently show the registration number and the authority's website, and agents must register before facilitating sales and must not facilitate unregistered projects. States add detail: MahaRERA requires a scannable QR code beside the number on ads, including agents' ads, and a certificate of competency for agent registration.

compliance.title: RERA: advance limit, quarterly disclosure and defect liability
compliance.description: A promoter may not take more than ten percent of a unit's cost as an advance or application fee before a written agreement for sale is registered, must update bookings, approvals and construction status on the authority's website every quarter, and must fix structural and workmanship defects reported within five years of possession. Our booking, update and snag workflows are designed around these duties; state rules and formats vary.

compliance.title: Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023 and DPDP Rules 2025
compliance.description: Buyer, tenant, partner and worker data is personal data under the DPDP Act. The Rules, notified in November 2025, phase in over eighteen months to May 2027: clear itemized notices, consent as easy to withdraw as to give, reasonable security safeguards with logs kept for a year, and breach intimation to affected people without delay with a detailed report to the Board within seventy-two hours. Bought or shared lead lists need a documented basis before outreach.

compliance.title: TRAI rules for calls and SMS, and WhatsApp messaging policy
compliance.description: Promotional calls and SMS follow TRAI's TCCCPR 2018 as amended in February 2025: registered headers and DLT templates for SMS, promotional calls only from 140-series numbers, no telemarketing from ordinary ten-digit numbers, and respect for customer preferences, in which real estate is a category people can block. WhatsApp requires an opt-in naming the business, approved templates outside the 24-hour service window and a clear route to a person.

compliance.title: Prevention of Money Laundering Act duties for real estate agents
compliance.description: Real estate agents as defined under RERA with annual turnover of twenty lakh rupees or more are notified as reporting entities under the PMLA, with CBIC named as their regulator. Duties include registering with FIU-IND, appointing a Principal Officer and Designated Director, verifying clients and beneficial owners, keeping records for five years and reporting suspicious transactions without tipping off the client. Confirm current thresholds and duties with your advisers.

compliance.title: Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code 2020
compliance.description: The OSH Code came into force on 21 November 2025 and subsumes the Building and Other Construction Workers Act 1996. Central Rules were notified in May 2026, while most private sites follow state rules issued on each state's timeline. Construction work with ten or more workers brings duties such as registration, commencement notices, prescribed registers and prompt notice of fatal accidents, serious injuries and dangerous occurrences such as a structure collapse.

faqs.question: Will an AI assistant quote prices, offers or possession dates to our buyers?
faqs.answer: No. Automated replies cover amenities, location, carpet areas, price ranges and documents only from content your team approves, including the RERA registration and project details. Specific prices come from the approved price sheet through your executive, and offers, discounts, payment-plan changes, possession dates and legal questions always go to a person. Your sales head and legal team approve the knowledge base and templates before launch.

faqs.question: Do we need to replace our CRM, ERP or site software?
faqs.answer: No. We connect to the systems you already run, such as Sell.Do, LeadSquared, Salesforce or Zoho CRM, Farvision, SAP or Tally, Yardi or Nexudus, and site apps, through their APIs, webhooks or approved exports. Where a system has no interface, we agree a safe interim route and state its limits. Your existing systems stay the source of truth.

faqs.question: Can we message portal leads on WhatsApp straight away?
faqs.answer: Only where the person has opted in to messages from your business. WhatsApp requires an opt-in that names the business and approved templates outside the 24-hour service window. Where a portal or form does not capture that opt-in, the assigned executive calls first and offers it. Promotional calls and SMS follow TRAI rules, including 140-series numbers for promotional calls, DLT-registered templates and the customer's real estate preference.

faqs.question: How do you settle channel partner disputes?
faqs.answer: We do not; your policy does. We turn your written rules, such as registration validity and what counts as a direct lead, into checks that timestamp every registration, visit and contact. Possible conflicts go to your channel partner manager with the full evidence timeline, and partners only ever see their own clients.

faqs.question: Many of our buyers are NRIs. What changes?
faqs.answer: Messages and follow-ups are scheduled in the buyer's local daytime, video site visits overlap with Indian working hours, and answers on eligibility and payments come only from an FAQ your legal team approves. Under RBI rules, NRIs and OCIs may buy property other than agricultural land, plantations and farmhouses, paying through banking channels or NRE, FCNR or NRO accounts. For buyers in the EU or UK the GDPR or UK GDPR may also apply, and Meta ads aimed at audiences in the US, Canada or parts of Europe may fall under its housing special ad category.

faqs.question: We are a contractor, not a developer. Is this relevant to us?
faqs.answer: Yes. Contractors usually start with RFQ and BOQ intake or one daily site report covering progress, labor and material requests, then add safety incident logging and snag rectification for clients. Site forms work offline on ordinary Android phones and sync when the connection returns, and approvals follow your own value limits.

faqs.question: How long does a first project take, and what drives the cost?
faqs.answer: A first pilot usually runs three to six weeks, depending mainly on CRM and portal access and template approvals. We quote after discovery, once your systems, volumes and existing licenses are known. Provider charges such as WhatsApp messaging, SMS, telephony and model usage are billed by those providers and shown separately.

faqs.question: Who owns the buyer, partner and site data?
faqs.answer: You do. We set up messaging, database and automation accounts in your organization's name wherever the provider allows, limit our access to named people for named tasks, and hand over credentials, documentation and workflows at the end of the engagement.
